enonce.texte:
Match the festival or celebration with its description.

FestivalDescription
ChristmasA Muslim celebration with prayer and feasting
EidA celebration of marriage between two people
New YearA Christian celebration of the birth of Jesus
WeddingThe first day of the year, celebrated with fireworks

questions.texte: Match each festival with its correct description.
questions.reponse: Christmas - A Christian celebration of the birth of Jesus; Eid - A Muslim celebration with prayer and feasting; New Year - The first day of the year, celebrated with fireworks; Wedding - A celebration of marriage between two people

sousQuestions.texte: Name another festival you know and describe it briefly.
sousQuestions.reponse: Example: 'Easter is a Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Jesus.'

enonce.texte: Look at the pictures and write the name of each festival or celebration in English.
images: A Christmas tree with gifts underneath.
A wedding ceremony with bride and groom.
Fireworks display for New Year's Eve.

questions.texte: Identify the festivals shown in the pictures.

enonce.texte:
Complete the sentences with used to or didn't use to + the verb in brackets.

  1. When I was a child, I ______ (celebrate) Christmas with my family.
  2. My grandmother ______ (cook) traditional dishes for Eid.
  3. I ______ (wear) formal clothes to weddings, but now I do.
  4. We ______ (watch) fireworks on New Year's Eve.

questions.texte: Fill in the blanks with the correct form of 'used to'.
questions.reponse: 1. used to celebrate, 2. used to cook, 3. didn't use to wear, 4. used to watch

sousQuestions.reponse: We use 'used to' to talk about past habits or actions that happened regularly in the past but no longer happen.

enonce.texte: Write a short paragraph (5-7 sentences) describing how you celebrate a festival in Cameroon. Use used to to talk about past celebrations and now for present celebrations.

questions.texte: Describe a festival celebration in Cameroon.
questions.reponse: Example: 'I used to celebrate Christmas in the village with my grandparents. We used to sing carols and eat special meals. Now, I celebrate Christmas in the city with my parents. We still cook traditional dishes. I used to receive small gifts, but now I give gifts to my younger cousins.'

enonce.texte:
You are organizing a festival celebration. Write a plan that includes:

  • The name of the festival
  • What you will do
  • What food you will serve
  • Who you will invite
  • How you used to celebrate this festival

questions.texte: Write a plan for a festival celebration.
questions.reponse: Example: 'I am organizing a New Year celebration. I will invite my family and friends. We will eat rice and chicken. I used to celebrate New Year by going to the beach, but now I celebrate at home with my family. We will watch fireworks at midnight and dance. I used to wear new clothes, and I will do the same this year.'

enonce.texte:
Choose the correct word to complete each sentence.

  1. We celebrate Christmas on ______ 25th. (December/January)
  2. Eid is a ______ festival. (Muslim/Christian)
  3. A ______ is a celebration of marriage. (wedding/birthday)
  4. On New Year's Eve, we watch ______. (fireworks/flowers)

questions.texte: Complete the sentences with the correct words.

enonce.texte:
Interview a classmate about a celebration they enjoy. Ask these questions and write their answers.

  • What is your favorite celebration?
  • How do you celebrate it?
  • What did you use to do differently?
  • Who do you celebrate with?

questions.texte: Write the interview questions and answers.
questions.reponse: Example: 'Q: What is your favorite celebration? A: My favorite celebration is Eid. Q: How do you celebrate it? A: I pray, visit family, and eat special food. Q: What did you use to do differently? A: I used to celebrate in the village, but now I celebrate in the city. Q: Who do you celebrate with? A: I celebrate with my family and friends.'

enonce.texte:
Correct the mistakes in these sentences about festivals and celebrations.

  1. I used to celebrated Christmas in the village.
  2. We don't used to watch fireworks.
  3. She celebrate her wedding next month.
  4. They used to went to church for Christmas.

questions.texte: Correct the mistakes in each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. I used to celebrate Christmas in the village. 2. We didn't use to watch fireworks. 3. She celebrates her wedding next month. 4. They used to go to church for Christmas.

sousQuestions.texte: Why is 'used to' followed by the base form of the verb?
sousQuestions.reponse: Because 'used to' is already in the past, the main verb remains in the base form.

intitule: Writing a Letter About a Festival

enonce.texte:
Write a letter to a pen pal in another country. Describe a festival you celebrate in Cameroon. Include:

  • The name of the festival
  • What you do
  • What you eat
  • How you used to celebrate it when you were younger
  • Why it is important to you

questions.texte: Write a letter to your pen pal describing a festival.
questions.reponse: Example: 'Dear Pen Pal, I want to tell you about Christmas in Cameroon. We celebrate Christmas with family and friends. We eat rice, chicken, and cake. We go to church and sing carols. When I was younger, I used to celebrate in the village with my grandparents. Now, I celebrate in the city. Christmas is important to me because we come together as a family. I hope you can come to Cameroon one day to celebrate with us. Best, [Your Name]'

enonce.texte:
Rewrite the sentences using used to or didn't use to.

  1. In the past, I lived in a small village. (now I live in the city)
  2. I played with my friends every day. (now I don't)
  3. We ate traditional food for every celebration. (now we eat different food)
  4. I was afraid of fireworks. (now I'm not)

questions.reponse: 1. I used to live in a small village. 2. I used to play with my friends every day. 3. We used to eat traditional food for every celebration. 4. I used to be afraid of fireworks.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the difference between 'used to' and 'would' for past habits?
sousQuestions.reponse: 'Used to' can describe states and habits, while 'would' is only for actions/habits in the past.
